messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: hosted-runtime kvcache memory spike on hosted-gpu-pool-2. metric=kvcache.mem_pct, value=94%, duration=7m. Symptoms: OOMs on workers, elevated 502s. Triage channel created.

maya: seeing rapid growth of KV keys for sessions tied to model redwood-v1-3b. long prompts + continuous prefetch seems to be creating sticky keys.

cal: confirmed, root cause looks like prefix amplification from a subset of customers sending concatenated transcripts. keys/sess jumped from ~120 to >3k in minutes.

jin: tagging @oncall and paging infra to throttle prefetch. oncall, can you cutoff prefetch globally?

oncall: I'm on it. Pushing emergency knob: PREFETCH_ENABLED=false to hosted runtime config for pool-2. Rolling via /api/internal/configs.

eli: hold - if we fully disable prefetch latency will spike across many requests. Suggest capping PREFETCH_MAX_KEYS=200 instead, and reduce CONTINUOUS_BATCH_SIZE=4.

sofia: customers impacted: 4 high-traffic customers saw 502 spikes and elevated latencies. Support flags: #customer-impact-board updated.

maya: agree with eli. Command to apply minimal-impact hotfix:

```bash
# apply env patch to pool-2
curl -X POST https://internal-config.redwood/api/v1/pools/hosted-gpu-pool-2/patch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"PREFETCH_MAX_KEYS":"200","CONTINUOUS_BATCH_SIZE":"4"}'
```

cal: running the patch now. will monitor kvcache.mem_pct and OOM counts.

incident-bot: Deploy initiated by cal at 3172223430. Change: PREFETCH_MAX_KEYS=200, CONTINUOUS_BATCH_SIZE=4.

maya: also kicking eviction for sessions older than 1h to reclaim hot keys.

jin: added a Kubernetes job to delete stale session prefixes from redis shard 3: `kubectl run evict-31722 --image=redis-tools -- redis-cli --scan --pattern "sess:*" | xargs redis-cli del` (dry-run first).

cal: patch applied. Observability: kvcache.mem_pct falling from 94% -> 78% in 2m. OOM count trending down. 502s reduced but still above baseline.

sofia: notifying affected customers A, B, C with interim message: "We've applied throttles to prefetch to reduce memory pressure; you may see slightly higher latency while we stabilize."

support-bot: Created ticket #INC-317222 for customer B, linked to this thread.

eli: can we add rule to runtime to ignore overly long single tokens in prefetch? That will prevent concatenated transcripts from exploding key count.

maya: quick mitigation: limit max prefix length to 8k tokens for prefetch. We'll follow up with longer-term change.

jin: adding alert override to avoid noisy paging once mem < 70% for 10m.

cal: mem_pct steady at ~65% now. OOMs zero in last 10m. Rolling back more aggressive caps? Recommend keep PREFETCH_MAX_KEYS=200 for next 6 hours while we run postmortem.

oncall: agreed. Handoff to daytime oncall @maya for monitoring. Leaving note in rotation: if mem_pct > 80% re-escalate immediately.

sofia: drafting comms for SRE and support: short incident summary + mitigation + customer impact (4 customers, partial 502s from 3172223300-3172223600 UTC).

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Next steps: run postmortem, implement prefix-length guard, evaluate continuous prefetch heuristics, and add test coverage for long prompt amplification.

maya: logging followups in backlog: (1) rate-limit prefetch per session (2) add unit test for concatenated transcripts (3) add eviction threshold config per-pool.

eli: will take the postmortem lead. Planning doc in #eng-postmortems.

cal: final note: thumbs up to quick config patch — low-risk and effective. Keep observing for 2 more hours. :thumbsup:
